newsitem.title: UK: VFG sets AIM debut for 27 February.
newsitem.headline: VFG sets AIM debut for 27 February.

text.p: VFG Plc, a broadcast video, film and grip equipment hire and sales company, said on Thursday it plans to float on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) on February 27.
The float follows a placing of shares at 40p by broker IA Pritchard, raising 3.0 million stg before expenses and valuing VFG at 5.7 million stg.

VFG, which supplies equipment for television programmes including Coronation Street, London Bridge and Hollyoaks, said it would invest 2.8 million stg in the latest generation of Sony digital cameras.

VFG, with offices in London, Manchester, Cardiff, Bristol and Shepperton, said its profit before tax and exceptional items had risen by 75 percent in the year ended 30 November 1996 to 281,000 stg, with turnover up 59 percent at 3.1 million.

The group said it had benefitted from the fragmentation and regionalisation of television production in the UK following the 1991 broadcasting act and earned an increasing amount of its income from independent production companies.

In addition to the hire of professional broadcast quality video, film and grip equipment, the company buys and sells new and used equipment both in the UK and abroad and operates as a sales and distribution agency.

The AIM listing will give greater access to capital and allow VFG, which said it was the fourth largest television production hire company in the UK, to increase its stocks of hire equipment and working capital.

Managing director Tony Covell said in a statement he had been delighted by the institutional support for the float and the issue would allow VFG to take advantage of the growth in television production.

"The funding of new equipment will allow us fully to take advantage of the exciting growth in the UK television production market, and in particular the continuing expansion of digital television production," he said.
